title: Small-scale randomness in the network makes space robustly 3D

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Small-scale randomness in the network makes space robustly 3D

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The ultimate rules for the universe will produce networks that look largely random at small scales, and this randomness is what allows a definite and robust dimensionality of 3 to emerge for space.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: my expectation is that they will give rise to networks that on a small scale look largely random. But this very randomness will most likely be what for example allows a definite and robust value of 3 to emerge for the dimensionality of space

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 9, “Fundamental Physics”; section “Evolution of Networks” (from p. 508), p. 515. Scope: network models of space and the dimensionality of physical space

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch09-19: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.37

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Computation can test a restricted mechanistic association, but not the claim about the universe's ultimate rules. Discriminating the proposed cause of three-dimensionality requires both sharper theory and new empirical access.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across a defined ensemble of network rules, quantify local randomness and large-scale volume-growth dimension, testing whether robust dimension three occurs specifically because of randomness. Physical support would additionally require signatures linking the successful ensemble to observed spacetime.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Simulation can show correlation but not that nature uses the mechanism.

No canonical rule ensemble or randomness metric.

Existing observations do not access the microscopic network.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: That physical space has three dimensions is already the working content of existing particle and cosmological data, so that fragment of the claim is settled. The further claim that small-scale network randomness is what makes dimension 3 robust is a mechanism, and published network samples are too few to separate it from rules that impose dimension directly.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure spatial dimension from large-scale physics, and separately evolve network rules with and without small-scale randomness, estimating dimension from node growth. Robust dimension 3 only in the random ensemble would support the mechanism; dimension 3 arising equally from ordered networks, or random networks failing to lock dimension 3, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Estimating a stable dimension on large random networks is a specialist computation, not a weeks-scale survey.

Many models set dimension to 3 directly, so the observed dimension does not show that randomness is the cause.

fields.value:
